content.prompt: Find the value(s) of $k$ for which the following have two distinct real roots.

inlines.text: and select the exterior intervals from the sketch of

answer.worked:
Two distinct real roots require $\Delta>0$.

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-k)^2-4(1)(-k)\\\Delta&=k^2+4k\\\Delta&=k(k+4)\end{align*}$$

The boundary values satisfy

$$\begin{align*}k(k+4)&=0\\k&=-4\text{ or }k=0.\end{align*}$$

Sketch $\Delta=k(k+4)$. The parabola opens upwards, so $\Delta>0$ outside its two roots. Hence $k<-4$ or $k>0$.

inlines.text: . Find the exact boundary values with the quadratic formula, then select the exterior intervals from the sketch.

answer.worked:
Two distinct real roots require $\Delta>0$.

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(1-k)^2-4(2)(k)\\\Delta&=k^2-10k+1\end{align*}$$

Find the boundary values using the quadratic formula:

$$\begin{align*}k^2-10k+1&=0\\k&=\frac{10\pm\sqrt{(-10)^2-4(1)(1)}}{2(1)}\\k&=\frac{10\pm\sqrt{96}}{2}\\k&=5\pm2\sqrt{6}.\end{align*}$$

Sketch $\Delta=k^2-10k+1$. The parabola opens upwards, so $\Delta>0$ outside its two roots. Hence $k<5-2\sqrt{6}$ or $k>5+2\sqrt{6}$.
